resonance.title: Resonance
resonance.author: Jihun Park
resonance.material: Spherical speaker, vibration, bone conduction, dynamic LED feedback
resonance.summary: A spherical speaker designed to be hugged, allowing music to be felt through the body as vibration, light, and intimate presence.

blocks.text: Resonance is a spherical speaker designed to be hugged, allowing users to feel music through their body using bone conduction and dynamic LED feedback. Beyond sound, it offers a multi-sensory emotional experience through vibration and light.

The project begins from the desire to make music more than a passive act of listening. By asking the listener to hold the speaker close, it shifts audio from a distant signal into something that can be felt physically and emotionally.

The form draws upon the metaphor of space. Space represents a place of emotional refuge, a quiet separation from reality, and a temporary room in which the listener can enter their own sonic universe.
By hugging the speaker, the user symbolically boards a tiny personal spaceship. The spacecraft form reflects a journey away from noise and toward the self.
The object does not simply deliver audio. It frames solitude as a designed condition, using light, surface, weight, and vibration to make inner attention visible.
Resonance offers not just sound, but an escape into feeling: a gift of presence, a moment of solitude, sound, and self-connection.

artifit.title: ARTIFIT
artifit.author: Changhyun Park
artifit.material: Wearable device, shelf, robotic arm, Bluetooth, pen drawing
artifit.summary: A fitness companion that translates workout intensity and motion into analog drawings made by a robotic arm.

blocks.text: ARTIFIT is a unique fitness companion combining a wearable device, a shelf, and a robotic arm to transform home workouts into an engaging artistic experience.
The wearable device monitors heart rate and motion, sending data via Bluetooth to the robotic arm, which then draws lines reflecting the user's exercise intensity and movement.
Inspired by interactive workout products like Ringfit, ARTIFIT replaces digital graphics with analog, tangible creativity, motivating users through the evolving artwork.
The system emphasizes fun, interaction, and recordkeeping by allowing users to change pen colors, track different exercises, and observe their workout's dynamic visual expression.
It aims to encourage those who find exercise boring by offering simple yet meaningful engagement without complex interfaces.
Future plans focus on enhancing the robotic arm's drawing capabilities, refining firmware for subtle motion capture, and conducting user feedback sessions to improve the overall experience.

calm.title: C.A.L.M
calm.author: Gaeheon Lee, Hyerin Na, Jungin Park, Hyungseok Moon, Yenglik Tleukulova
calm.material: AI-moderated debate, legal guidance, proposal summary interface
calm.summary: Civic AI Law Moderator that supports public participation in legislative proposals through AI-moderated debates and concise outcome summaries.

blocks.text: C.A.L.M is a Civic AI Law Moderator that empowers users to engage with and refine legislative proposals through AI-moderated debates, on-demand legal guidance, and concise outcome summaries.

The project addresses the difficulty of public participation in legal discussion, where ordinary voices are often filtered by specialized language, institutional distance, or the fear of speaking incorrectly.
By structuring discussion into guided turns, the system allows disagreement to remain productive while helping participants understand the legal and social consequences of a proposal.
Its moderation does not replace civic judgment. Instead, it provides a shared surface where arguments can be clarified, condensed, compared, and returned to the group.

The phrase 'Everyone's voice has a right to be understood' becomes both a service promise and a design constraint, asking the interface to make complexity more approachable without flattening difference.
C.A.L.M imagines legislation not as a remote expert procedure, but as a public conversation whose quality depends on the tools through which people learn to listen.

photo-techniques.title: ID218 Photo Techniques
photo-techniques.author: Eun-woo Kang, Na-eun Kim, Yu-na Kim, So-hyun Park, Jung-won Park, In-sung Seo, Yoon-ho Wang, Si-yoon Yoo, Jae-yong Lee, Jun-hyun Lee, Jin-woo Lee, Hyun-jun Jung, Chang-won Choi
photo-techniques.material: Manual camera operation, studio lighting, scientific imaging, image generation
photo-techniques.summary: A course exhibition exploring photography as technical reproduction, visual language, and a framework for expanded creative practice.

blocks.text: Photography extends beyond technical reproduction and functions as a critical visual language through which the ontological and socio-cultural meanings of images can be explored.
This course aims to establish a systematic understanding of photographic techniques while examining aesthetic experiences through the frameworks of photographic philosophy and media aesthetics.
In response to rapidly evolving media environments, the course integrates AI-based image generation technologies into photographic practice.
The practical component emphasizes manual camera operation to develop an understanding of optical principles and exposure control.
Students work with studio lighting techniques that investigate the sculptural and narrative qualities of light, connecting technical control to expressive intention.

The course also introduces scientific imaging through electron microscopy and creative production using AI generators, fostering experimental methodologies that integrate traditional techniques with emerging technologies.

handheld-product.title: Handheld Product Project
handheld-product.author: Department of Industrial Design
handheld-product.material: Geometric primitives, organic surfaces, handheld product redesign
handheld-product.summary: A basic design project exploring the intersection of geometric clarity, organic transformation, and usability through handheld product forms.

blocks.text: Handheld product project is a final project guiding students to explore the intersection of geometric clarity and organic transformation through the redesign of a hair dryer.
Starting with two or three basic geometric primitives such as cones, cylinders, or cubes, students create dynamic compositions by joining them with exaggerated organic surfaces.
Before the handheld product project, students explore pure geometric composition with rectangular volumes to create a sense of balance, tension, and overall aesthetics.
The project brings in the elements of utility and usability while still retaining balance and tension in form-giving with the purity of geometry.
By compressing a functional object into a controlled formal exercise, the course asks students to negotiate between abstract composition and embodied use.
This project gives an opportunity to study how a handheld object can remain practical while carrying a precise visual argument about proportion, surface, and transformation.

niche-prize.title: The Niche Prize Awards
niche-prize.author: Department of Industrial Design
niche-prize.material: CAD, symbolic trophy, personal narrative, 3D print
niche-prize.summary: A fictional award project translating personal passions and overlooked values into symbolic trophy forms.

blocks.text: The Niche Prize Awards is a midterm design project where students were asked to create a fictional award that represents their personal area of highest interest.
Each student designs a symbolic trophy to visualize the meaning of the award, turning an individual interest into a physical object that can be publicly displayed.
Each trophy on display reflects a personal narrative, celebrating the overlooked, the unconventional, and the deeply individual.
From defining the award's purpose and values to constructing its visual identity, students explore how meaning can be embedded in design through CAD.
This project reframes CAD not just as a technical skill, but as a medium for translating identity, emotion, and values into physical form.
The resulting objects make the invisible visible: a small private attachment becomes a public sign, and a personal passion takes on the posture of an official prize.

object-01.title: Altered Seeing
object-01.author: Department of Industrial Design
object-01.material: Exhibition text, mobile browser, reading duration, collective display
object-01.summary: A prototype guide that uses the familiar form of exhibition interpretation to observe how reading itself becomes part of the installation.

blocks.text: This guide follows the language of the permanent exhibition: a title on the left, a project description on the right, and the quiet authority of a label that asks to be trusted.
The interface does not introduce itself as an experiment. It borrows the dry surface of institutional explanation so that reading can proceed without theatrical emphasis.
Each paragraph becomes a small sensor of attention. The text is not only displayed on the screen; it is measured by the time it remains visible, the depth of a scroll, and the moment of return.
In the exhibition space, this creates a second layer of looking. Visitors believe they are reading about objects, while their reading slowly creates another object elsewhere in the room.
The most persistent sentences become heavier, darker, and more central. Others fade before they are remembered, leaving a landscape shaped by collective trust.
What remains at the end is not a dashboard of visitors, but a text formed by reading: an image of how explanation can become material.
